from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Review: The Standard Infinite Sum", [
            "Standard sums grow, racing toward infinity.", 
            "We add terms like 1, 2, 4, 8.", 
            "The pile grows infinitely large."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        math_expr = MathTex(r"\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} 2^n = 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + \dots", font_size=40)
        self.place_at_grid(math_expr, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        terms = VGroup(*[MathTex(str(2**i)) for i in range(4)])
        for i, term in enumerate(terms):
            self.place_at_grid(term, f'D{i+1}', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        pile = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(pile, 'F3', scale_factor=1.0)
        pile_label = Text("Sum", font_size=20).next_to(pile, UP)
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(math_expr), FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(t) for t in terms], lag_ratio=0.5))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.play(GrowFromCenter(pile), Write(pile_label))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFA500")
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "The sum 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 converges.",
            "Each step brings us nearer to negative one.",
            "Distance shrinks, settling onto the value.",
            "It does not fly away to infinity.",
            "2-adic space defies our Euclidean intuition."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Counter-Intuitive Convergence", lecture_lines)
        
        # Visuals

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Philosophical Implication", [
            "Real and 2-adic distances differ fundamentally.",
            "Distance is defined by our chosen metric.",
            "The world changes with the lens used."
        ])
        
        # Visualization objects
        euclidean_label = Text("Euclidean", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        padic_label = Text("2-adic", color=WHITE, font_size=24)
        
        self.place_at_grid(euclidean_label, "A2")
        self.place_at_grid(padic_label, "A5")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Recap core concepts visually
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        circle_real = Circle(radius=0.5, color=WHITE).shift(self.grid["C2"])
        circle_padic = Circle(radius=0.5, color=WHITE).shift(self.grid["C5"])
        
        self.play(Create(circle_real), Create(circle_padic))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show convergence versus divergence comparison
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FA9A")
        
        line_div = Line(start=self.grid["D2"], end=self.grid["E2"], color=RED)
        dot_conv = Dot(self.grid["E5"], color=GREEN)
        
        self.play(Create(line_div), FadeIn(dot_conv))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Present concluding thought on infinite sets
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#87CEEB")
        
        lens_frame = Rectangle(height=2, width=3, color=BLUE).move_to(self.grid["E3"])
        self.play(FadeIn(lens_frame))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The 2-adic Metric: Redefining Distance in Infinite Sums

sections.title: Review: The Standard Infinite Sum
sections.content: Briefly revisit real-number convergence. Explain that in standard Euclidean space, 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + ... diverges to infinity because the 'size' of terms grows. Use a visual 'number line' where points fly off to the right.
sections.example: A squirrel gathering acorns: if the squirrel adds exponentially more acorns every day, its pile grows infinitely large.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Changing the 'Lens' of Distance
sections.content: Introduce the 2-adic valuation: $|x|_2$. In this metric, a number is 'small' if it is divisible by a high power of 2. Visual: Instead of a number line, use a tree diagram (fractal structure) where numbers sharing powers of 2 are clustered together.
sections.example: A magical 'divisibility filter' that makes 8 (2^3) 'smaller' than 2 (2^1) because 8 is more divisible by 2.

sections.title: The Counter-Intuitive Convergence
sections.content: Show the sum S = 1 + 2 + 4 + 8 + ... in the 2-adic metric. Demonstrate that as we add more terms, the 'distance' between partial sums and the value -1 becomes 0. Use an animation of the sum 'shrinking' toward the center of the 2-adic disk.
sections.example: A robotic arm moving in a 2-adic space: with each step (adding powers of 2), it doesn't move further away, but rather settles precisely onto the coordinate -1.

sections.title: Summary & Philosophical Implication
sections.content: Conclude by comparing real convergence (based on magnitude) vs. p-adic convergence (based on divisibility). Emphasize that the definition of 'close' is subjective to the metric chosen.
sections.example: A character choosing between two maps: one map shows distance by physical miles (Euclidean), the other by shared prime factors (2-adic).
